;Arts and culture
*A team of ocean explorers announce the discovery of [[Empire of Japan|Imperial Japanese]] [[aircraft carrier]] ''[[Japanese aircraft carrier Akagi|Akagi]]'' on the [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific]] seafloor. The vessel was sunk in 1942 during the [[World War II]] [[Battle of Midway]]. *A fiery bus crash near [[Kinshasa]] in [[the Democratic Republic of Congo]] kills at least 31 people, with another 18 injured. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/21/africa/congo-bus-fire-intl/index.html (CNN)]
;International relations
*[[New Zealand–United Kingdom relations]]
**The Foreign Minister of New Zealand [[Winston Peters]] accuses the [[United Kingdom]] of "walking out" on Pacific aid to small island nations. The accusation surprised British officials. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/401460/uk-walked-out-on-pacific-nz-s-foreign-minister (Radio New Zealand)]

;Law and crime
*[[Murder of Ján Kuciak]]
**Authorities in [[Slovakia]] charge four people with murdering investigative journalist Ján Kuciak and his fiancée. The killings sparked widespread anti-corruption protests and forced the resignation of [[Prime Minister of Slovakia|Prime Minister]] [[Robert Fico]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/21/slovakia-four-people-charged-murder-investigative-journalist-jan-kuciak (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-slovakia-crime/four-charged-in-slovak-journalist-murder-that-brought-down-prime-minister-idUSKBN1X011E?fbclid=IwAR2GsTW39FVTcE0vLf1xn8Sw78S3JuXFZ7OhfsAE1qOSVnvtIi7H8E7a7-Y (Reuters)]
*[[Opioid epidemic in the United States]]
**[[Teva Pharmaceuticals]], [[McKesson]], and [[AmerisourceBergen]] reach a {{usd}}260 million settlement hours before a civil trial in [[U.S. federal court]] in [[Cleveland]], [[Ohio]], brought as a class-action lawsuit representing communities affected by opioid addiction. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/oct/21/opioid-makers-drug-industry-trial-cleveland-ohio (''The Guardian'')] [https://theweek.com/speedreads/873162/drug-companies-reach-settlement-ohio-counties-avoid-federal-opioid-trial (''The Week'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Canadian federal election]]
**Voters in [[Canada]] go to the polls to elect members of the 43rd Canadian Parliament. Polls show [[Justin Trudeau]]'s [[Liberal Party of Canada|Liberals]] and [[Andrew Scheer]]'s [[Conservative Party of Canada|Conservatives]] deadlocked with equal numbers of support after a divisive campaign. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/grenier-polls-election-end-1.5327737 (CBC News)] [https://election.ctvnews.ca/frantic-final-push-for-votes-marks-final-day-of-divisive-campaign-1.4646693 (CTV News)] [https://www.huffpost.com/entry/canada-votes-in-election-that-could-see-justin-trudeau-lose-power_n_5dadc3d0e4b0422422c91c62?fbclid=IwAR1Z_uGBww69lD5wGK8UEjC4SfgrXohTIvMgoiJ_58wNxGyh2R7bWdKqZMU (''HuffPost'')]
**The Liberal Party win a pluralty of seats, and will remain in government, albeit as a [[minority government|minority]] and having lost the popular vote to the Conservative Party. The [[Bloc Québécois]] resurge from a 10-seat rump at dissolution to take third place and regain [[official party status]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/federal-election-results-2019-cbc-leaders-1.5329485 (CBC News)] [https://election.ctvnews.ca/trudeau-nabs-minority-government-loses-the-popular-vote-in-tumultuous-campaign-1.4649117 (CTV News)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2019/10/22/canadian-pm-justin-trudeaus-liberals-to-form-minority-government-cbc.html?fbclid=IwAR2PWNKinwA28zkBnZMZ0WVPVPlNCjTtvB8halERy_1AXme5HLfo4GR5bV8 (CNBC)]
*[[2019 Chilean protests]]
**[[Chilean President]] [[Sebastián Piñera]] says that Chile is "at war" and calls on citizens to take sides in the matter as violence continues in the capital and other cities.
